title: Scalar-Tensor Hydrodynamics: Gravity as the Response of a Vacuum Medium. A Modified Gravity Framework for Vacuum Viscosity and Cyclic Vacuum Cosmology
description:
A theoretical proposal built on one premise: there is no empty space. The vacuum is treated as a single continuous medium, the Ocean, with its own stress-energy, pressure, internal flow and dissipative response, and with no edges and no outside. What are conventionally called particles are treated as localized excitations of the medium, and gravity is proposed to be the medium's response to concentrated energy. Einstein's equation is retained as the effective description of that response.

The formalism adds to the Einstein tensor a dynamical scalar-field sector, a vacuum viscous stress, a field-dependent pressure in place of a fixed cosmological constant, and a state-dependent effective coupling. A refractive account of gravity is stated together with its decisive tests: every excitation must respond in exactly the same proportion, time must slow and space stretch in equal measure, and gravitational waves must travel at the speed of light.

The matter sector is partitioned by a localization criterion derived from the medium's own excitation spectrum. The crossover is set by the healing length, which recovers the electron rest energy as a calibration rather than an input. A cyclic Heartbeat cosmology is treated separately within the present beat and across beats, and the galactic sector, black holes and the vacuum effects already measured at the electron scale are addressed.

This is a proposal, not an established theory. The document states its own falsification conditions explicitly and carries an itemized research program, several items of which could terminate the framework.
